name: Heritable Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) Guidelines for Pulmonary Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Presence of a first-degree relative with confirmed pulmonary arterial hypertension or known pathogenic mutation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with heritable PAH (e.g., BMPR2, ALK1, ENG)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hemodynamic criteria confirmed by right heart catheterization plus exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension; family history or genetic confirmation supports diagnosis of heritable PAH.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other forms of pulmonary hypertension and comprehensive clinical evaluation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exertional dyspnea due to elevated pulmonary arterial pressure
searchTerms: dyspnea due to high lung pressure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Syncope on exertion related to right ventricular failure
Progressive fatigue secondary to reduced cardiac output
searchTerms: feeling very tired due to weak heart

common.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to right heart failure
searchTerms: swelling in legs from heart problems
ankle puffiness due to heart failure

occasional.symptomName: Hemoptysis from pulmonary artery rupture or vascular remodeling
searchTerms: bloody sputum from lung vessel damage
blood in cough due to lung issues

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to hepatic congestion
searchTerms: abdominal distension due to liver backup

occasional.symptomName: Jugular venous distension indicating right heart strain
Raynaud phenomenon associated with connective tissue disease overlap
searchTerms: fingers turning white or blue in cold
poor blood flow to fingers in cold
skin turning blue from low oxygen
bluish discoloration due to low blood oxygen

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure
fits due to lack of oxygen to brain

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: Right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation on echocardiography
Enlarged pulmonary arteries on chest CT or chest X-ray
Perfusion defects on ventilation-perfusion scan excluding thromboembolic disease
other: Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure
Exclusion of secondary causes of pulmonary hypertension (e.g., left heart disease, lung disease)

distinguishingFeatures: No family history or identifiable genetic mutation
Similar hemodynamic profile but sporadic occurrence
Elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (>15 mmHg)
Echocardiographic evidence of left heart dysfunction
History of pulmonary embolism or thrombosis

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure with peripheral edema and ascites
Severe hypoxemia or cyanosis at rest
references: Simonneau G, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019.
Rich S, et al. Primary pulmonary hypertension: clinical features. Chest. 1987.
